messages.subject: Discrete alpha values work around
parts:
I'm generating stimuli for an experiment and my goal is to make a plot that looks like the following. 




Here is my data, theme, and plot
#data
Ten_OneSDdata.frame(measure=rnorm(500, 10, 1), data_points="10")
Ten_OneSD_Quant<- data.frame(quantile(Ten_OneSD$measure, probs = c(.33, .66)))
Ten_OneSD$LowerQ<-Ten_OneSD_Quant[1,1]
Ten_OneSD$UpperQ<-Ten_OneSD_Quant[2,1]
Ten_OneSDB<-Ten_OneSD 
Ten_OneSDB$AB<-"B"
Ten_OneSD$AB<-"A"
Prob<-data.frame(measure = (10), data_points= "1", LowerQ=0, UpperQ=0, AB="AB")
Ten_One<- rbind(Ten_OneSD, Prob, Ten_OneSDB)

#theme
plain <- theme(panel.background = element_blank(),
               panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
               panel.grid.minor.x = element_blank(),
               panel.grid.minor.y = element_blank(),
               legend.position = "none", 
               axis.title.y=element_blank()
)

#plot
p <- ggplot(Ten_One, aes(x=AB, y=mean(measure), fill=AB)) + 
  geom_bar(position=position_dodge(), stat="identity", width = .5) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin=LowerQ, ymax=UpperQ, color = AB), width=.1, position=position_dodge(.9))+
  scale_fill_manual(values=c("white", "white", "grey"))+
  scale_color_manual(values=c("white","white", "black"))+
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(6, 15))+
  labs(x = "Bars indicate 66% likelihood of any data point falling withing the bounds", y="means")+
  geom_point(aes(x=AB, y=measure, alpha=AB, shape = factor(AB), size= factor(AB)),stroke=2, position = position_jitterdodge())+
  scale_alpha_discrete(range = c(1, .0))+
  scale_shape_manual(values =c(20, 4, 6))+
  scale_size_manual(values =c(.2, 4, .3))+
  scale_x_discrete(labels=c("A" = "A", "AB" = "Probe", "B" = "B"))+
  plain 
p

The resulting plot looks like this: (Notice that the gemo_points are solid resulting in over plotting)




The issue comes from not being able to set specific values for alpha or to set a color to transparency. 
My approach for generating the data and subsequent plot was to:
1. generate a normal distribution (see A) 
2. duplicate the distribution (see B)
3. generate a random value from the previous distribution parameters (see Probe)
4. plot the distributions with both points and bars 
5. make the background white and one of the bars white 
6. change the alpha of the points so that one group would be set to alpha=.0

Now I'm stuck and can't add another alpha value to the Y values or change the order of X values because the "Probe" point needs to go in the middle.
Thoughts?

PS. Hadley if you are out there, it would be really great to be able to explicitly set alpha values. Warmly, Lace

messages.author: bfc2eb6b71169017
messages.subject: Re: Discrete alpha values work around
parts:
Barplots should be used for count data. You are trying to present some statistic within some margin (sd, CI...). My suggestion would be to use something like geom_pointrange().

Cheers,
Roman

messages.subject: Re: Discrete alpha values work around
parts:
Hi Lace,

I think you might be able to get what you want by restructuring your data
set. If it looks like this:

Ten <- data.frame(A_measure=c(rnorm(500, 10, 1),NA,NA),
AB_measure=c(rep(NA,500),10,NA),
B_measure=c(rep(NA,501),10),
LowerQ=c(rep(NA,501),9), # for example, but could obviously be the
quantile
UpperQ=c(rep(NA,501),11),
AB=c(rep("A",500),"AB","B") )

So that the data for each of A, B and AB are separate (as you want a
couple of types of graph and don't want an alpha applied to the AB point),
then:

p<-ggplot(Ten)+
geom_bar(aes(x=AB,y=B_measure,fill=AB),
position=position_dodge(),
stat="identity",width=0.5)+
geom_errorbar(aes(x=AB, ymin=LowerQ, ymax=UpperQ, color = AB),
width=.1, position="dodge")+
scale_fill_manual(values=c(NA,NA,"grey"))+
scale_colour_manual(values=c(NA,NA,"black"))+
geom_point(aes(x=AB,y=AB_measure),size=4,shape=4)+
geom_point(aes(x=AB,y=A_measure),size=1,alpha=0.25,position="jitter")

should get you started.

While I've used geom_bar here, I agree with Roman that something like
geom_pointrange would be preferable to geom_bar.

Regards,
Ron.
